title: Decompose rendering pipeline and keyboard-first accessibility for large time-series
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Re-architect the time-series chart rendering path to separate compositing layers (grid/axes, bulk series geometry, interactive hotspots/annotations, overlay controls) so we can use canvas for heavy geometry while preserving DOM/SVG for keyboard/focusable elements and accessible summaries. Provide keyboard-first interactions (focusable scrub control, keyboard pan/zoom, time-snap announcements) and an aria-live summarizer for screen reader users. Target large-series workloads (10k+ points) while keeping frame times under 16ms for core interactions on typical enterprise laptops.
acceptance_criteria: Render pipeline split implemented: axes/grid layer (SVG/CSS), series geometry layer (offscreen canvas), hotspot layer (SVG/DOM) — documented and toggled via feature flag
Keyboard-first controls: chart can be focused, left/right arrows move a scrubber with snap-to-nearest-point behavior; PageUp/PageDown jumps by visible window; Home/End to jump to bounds
Aria announcements: aria-live region provides a concise summary when scrubber moves (timestamp + primary series value) and when pan/zoom exceeds thresholds
Performance: for a 10k-point series on a M1-equivalent device, initial paint <= 120ms and interactive scrub response <= 16ms for keyboard moves
Hit testing: hotspot layer uses spatial index for O(log n) lookup and reports consistent focus order for keyboard navigation
Design review sign-off from PM and Eng and a green CI GitHub PR that introduces the feature flag and tests
design_notes: Trade-off: canvas for bulk geometry yields the best draw performance but is not keyboard-accessible — solved by a separate lightweight SVG/DOM overlay that mirrors interactive points for focus and semantics.
We will use an offscreen canvas (worklet/worker) where available to avoid main-thread rasterization spikes; fallback to main-thread canvas for legacy browsers.
Hit-testing: use a quadtree spatial index updated on data changes; on pan/zoom we reuse index transforms rather than rebuilding.
Accessibility: keep summaries short (<= 120 chars) and add a user preference toggle to disable live announcements for users who prefer silence.
Visual tokens: respect high-contrast tokens and increased text-size tokens from the design system; focus rings follow tokenized focus-outline styles.
Animations: reduce motion for users with prefers-reduced-motion; keyboard moves should be instant or low-latency step animations.
Fallback: when using the canvas path, ensure an SVG snapshot (for pointer semantics) exists for QA and screen reader testing in the test harness.
decisions: 2026-02-24: Chosen architecture approved — split layers + canvas geometry + SVG hotspot overlay (approved by Alex Kim - PM, Priya Nair - Eng)
Use quadtree spatial index (versus linear scan) to keep hit tests performant on dense series (decision by Jordan Lee - Designer and Soham Rao - Eng)
Offscreen canvas in a worker where available; polyfill falls back to main-thread canvas (approved to avoid blocking rollout)
Keyboard mapping: left/right = step, shift+left/right = 10-step, page up/down = jump by visible window, home/end = start/end (consensus from accessibility review)
Aria pattern: concise aria-live="polite" summary updates instead of verbose point-by-point feed to avoid screen reader spam
progress_updates: 2026-02-05: Initial prototype of split layers (SVG + canvas) built — demo recorded and posted to drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcDEF_example

2026-02-16: Engineering prototype benchmark: 10k points draw time reduced from 420ms to 95ms using offscreen canvas (ENG-4125). Benchmark notes: https://internal.redwood.ai/benchmarks/charting/2026-02

2026-02-24: Design review completed; requested microcopy changes for aria announcements and an explicit toggle in Console's chart preferences — review notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UI/Timeseries+Render+Decomposition
2026-03-02: Accessibility audit (internal) found that focus order on hotspots needed normalization; eng to add stable id generation for points before overlay mirroring (PR referenced below).
2026-03-08: First implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1489 — contains feature flag 'chart.splitRenderV2' and unit tests for keyboard scrub behavior
2026-03-10: QA pass in staging: keyboard navigation works across screens, but performance regression in Safari when offscreen canvas polyfill used — follow-up assigned to ENG-4189.
reviewers_feedback: Alex Kim (PM): 'Love the separation — please ensure the user preference to silence announcements is in the same settings panel as other chart toggles.'
Priya Nair (Eng): 'Spatial index approach looks good; add telemetry hooks to measure average hit-test time and scrub latency.'
Samira Ortiz (Accessibility): 'Announce only on discrete keyboard steps; avoid announcing during continuous pointer scrubbing. Provide an option to read a fuller context (multi-series) on demand.'
attachments: Figma frames for keyboard states and focus treatment: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/Charting-Keyboard-A11y
